title: Grateful Dead Live at The Matrix on 1966-12-01
lineage: SBD > Rm > Reel > DAT > CD > wav > SHN v3

ai_review.summary: Soundboard tape of the early‑60s garage‑blues Dead with rough mid‑60s fidelity, but highlighted by a scorching “Yonder’s Wall” (likely featuring Paul Butterfield) and classic Alice D. performance.
ai_review.review: This recording captures the raw, electric blues energy of the Dead in late‑1966 – Jerry’s guitar pops, Pigpen’s soulful organ/harmonica work (and possibly a guest Paul Butterfield) drive the set.  The soundboard source is typical of the era: lo‑fi and a bit muddy, yet it preserves the vibe of an electrifying early show.  Fans repeatedly point to “Yonder’s Wall,” “Alice D.,” “Me & My Uncle” and “Viola Lee” as standout moments.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviewers praise the musical performance (average ~4‑5 stars) while noting only modest recording flaws; weighted blend yields a solid >4 rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Typical mid‑60s tape sound – limited clarity, some hiss and drop‑outs, not crisp but authentic to the era; several reviewers call it "stinky" or "thin" yet still listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early garage‑blues set that moves smoothly through high‑energy blues numbers; the band is tight and soulful despite raw recording, giving a consistent, driving flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar described as having a nice pop and raucous, powerful tone throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ/harmonica work is highlighted as gritty and soulful; several reviewers think Paul Butterfield guests on harp for Yonder's Wall.
